## Unified alert policies and automation

- Alert lifecycle state now has one durable PostgreSQL owner with typed
  condition, metric, and occurrence rules; explicit Trigger and Resolve gates;
  immutable evidence; generic `alert.triggered` and `alert.resolved` edges; and
  deterministic recovery, scope, timer, and retry behavior.
- Alert-event schedules and webhooks use the same canonical event vocabulary.
  Schedules accept direct argv arrays with exact element-by-element rendering,
  while cron and job dispatch expose the same parsed-command inspection model.
- The console and operator documentation now cover complete rule syntax,
  timing semantics, deduplication, direct argv, selector review, and practical
  offline, saturation, traffic-cycle, recovery, and failed-job workflows.

## Bounded control-plane load

- Fleet snapshots, Monitoring cards, Overview, and the combined Home snapshot
  now share identical in-flight reads, bound distinct heavy work, preserve
  last-known data during admission pressure, and coalesce hidden-tab and
  event-driven refreshes.
- Current-cycle traffic accounting uses an exact transactional hourly ledger
  with a bounded raw tail and a complete raw-data fallback whenever coverage
  is incomplete or a cycle is not hour-aligned.
- Agent telemetry starts on a stable distributed phase and skips missed bursts;
  gateway telemetry admission is bounded and observable without blocking
  lifecycle or command traffic.
- Alert triage supports atomic, revision-checked batches of up to 1,000 alerts
  in one request, including deterministic locking, all-or-none audit records,
  and conflict-safe UI recovery.
- Refreshed data grids preserve their current page when the refreshed result
  still contains it, avoiding disruptive jumps during routine reconciliation.

## Verification

- The API, worker, agent, gateway, CLI, frontend, desktop/mobile UI, and
  multi-browser load paths were exercised with focused regression gates.
